reason: Verified in source and reproduced by driving the master. Source: line 254 is the ONLY writer of data-stack, and it lives inside closeRun(), which fires when a run ENDS - i.e. after every row in that run has already been measured at lines 287-290. So the measuring loop's `copy.getBoundingClientRect().height` and `el.getAttribute("data-stack") === "follow" ? 1 : 10` both read last render's grouping. On the render that CREATES a pair the leader is measured without the 12px `.b-item[data-stack="lead"] .b-copy { padding-bottom: var(--gap-snug) }` it is about to receive, so `bottom` is 12px short and the follower's push is 12px short. Driven (chromium, 1440x960, state=owner-editing, one press of 'Move a week earlier' - the gate's own scenario): the follower lands at --push 90px, .b-copy top 660.28 against the leader's .b-copy bottom 661.47 - the boxes overlap by 1.19px and the follower's hairline border-top sits 10.8px under the leader's text instead of 22.8px. It does NOT self-correct: still 90px after 700ms. Then a 1px window resize with zero data change (setViewportSize 1440->1439, nothing else touched) recomputes it to --push 102px, top 672.28, and the row moves down 12px within 60ms. That correction is not the declared motion: only `top` is transitioned (0.22s); --push drives `transform: translateY()`, which is in no transition list, so the row snaps instantly - identically under prefers-reduced-motion (measured both ways). Any later event does it - fonts.ready, opening the editor, the next press, a settle(). Not caught by either gate and not a restatement of one: collisions() at interaction-check.mjs:165 explicitly filters `data-stack !== "follow"` out of the rects it compares, and the six stacked-pair assertions (2311-2325) test pair count, attribute string, mark/count visibility, the said sentence and offsetTop - never the gap between the two copy blocks. Initial mount escapes because render-core settles twice (rAF then fonts.ready), which is precisely why the static frames look right and the interaction does not. No constraint is touched: no colour, no weight, no architecture, and this is layout correctness, not the out-of-scope performance work. The fix cannot make it worse - grouping depends only on data-away and the already-sorted `items` array, never on geometry, so hoisting it above the measuring loop is a pure ordering correction with no circularity and no extra layout thrash beyond the getBoundingClientRect already in the loop.
sharpenedFix: In place(), after the sort and the reparent flush, run one grouping pass over `items` before any measurement: walk the array, compare data-away with the previous row, and write data-stack ("" / "lead" / "follow") and the .b-unitSaid sentence ("first/then of N moments on this day") for every run. Then run the existing placement loop unchanged - it now reads a data-stack that is true for THIS render. Delete `run`, closeRun() and its trailing call. Two additions to interaction-check.mjs, because the existing stacked-pair block is attribute-only: (1) after the single press that forms the pair, measure the real vertical gap between the lead .b-copy's bottom and the follower .b-copy's top and require it positive (~10.8px, not -1.19); (2) a general idempotency assertion that is stronger than a resize probe - snapshot every row's --push, call window.__TLD.b.settle() with no data change, and require the snapshot identical. place() must be a fixed point; that one assertion closes this whole class of stale-attribute reads rather than only this instance.
